Classify recent hybrids individually

Source: R/classify.R
classify_hybrids.Rd

Tests each animal against the pure, first- and second-generation hybrid classes and second backcrosses. Each class is a pair of parents, each passing on species-2 alleles with a set probability: 0 (pure species 1), 1 (pure species 2), 0.5 (F1 or F2 parent), 0.25 or 0.75 (first backcross parent). For each animal the likelihood of its genotypes under every class is compared with the best fit under any pair of parental ancestries. If no class fits (likelihood-ratio test at alpha), the animal is called a later-generation hybrid.

Usage

classify_hybrids(
  scores,
  alpha = 0.01,
  error = 0.005,
  genotypes = NULL,
  markers = NULL,
  effective_markers = NULL,
  het_dropout = 0
)

Arguments

scores

Output of hybrid_scores() (S, H, n_markers).

alpha

Significance level of the fit test.

error

Genotyping error rate, or "estimate" (with genotypes). An estimate that reaches the top of its range (0.1) gives a warning: with many linked markers, extra variation in heterozygosity can be taken for genotyping error, and a fixed rate is then safer.

genotypes

Optional genotypes at the diagnostic markers, counting species-2 alleles, as from orient_genotypes(), one row per row of scores.

markers

Output of diagnostic_markers() matching the columns of genotypes (columns freq1 and freq2 are used).

effective_markers

Optional number of effectively independent markers. Markers on the same chromosome are inherited in blocks, so they carry less independent information than their number suggests. With this, log-likelihoods are scaled by effective_markers / n_markers (a composite-likelihood adjustment). The best class is unchanged, but animals are no longer rejected from every class just because their markers come in blocks. See effective_markers().

het_dropout

Probability that a heterozygote is called homozygous (allele dropout, common in reduced-representation sequencing). It is not estimated, because heterozygosity lost to dropout cannot be told apart from heterozygosity lost to inbreeding one animal at a time; set it from replicate genotyping or known error rates.

Value

scores with columns class (best class or "later"), probability (of the best class among the tested classes) and fit_p (p-value of the fit test). With error = "estimate", attribute error holds the estimated rate.

Details

With genotypes and markers, the likelihood uses each marker's allele frequencies in the two reference groups, so markers that are nearly but not perfectly fixed are handled correctly, as in NewHybrids (Anderson and Thompson 2002) and HIest (Fitzpatrick 2012). A parent with species-2 ancestry a passes on the species-2 allele at marker l with probability a * freq2[l] + (1 - a) * freq1[l]. The genotyping error rate can be estimated from the data (error = "estimate"). Without them, markers are treated as fixed and only the genotype counts implied by S and H are used.

Several third-generation classes are indistinguishable from earlier ones at unlinked markers whatever the number of markers: F1 x F2 and F2 x F2 look like F2, and F2 x pure looks like a first backcross. Inbreeding (related parents) lowers heterozygosity and moves animals off every class, so they are called later-generation hybrids. Use estimate_history() for populations of advanced hybrids. Markers must be diagnostic in the populations that actually hybridized, not only in the reference samples: a marker at which one source population carries the "wrong" allele makes its hybrids look like no class.

References

Anderson EC, Thompson EA (2002) A model-based method for identifying species hybrids using multilocus genetic data. Genetics 160:1217-1229.

Examples

ex <- hybridclock_example()
mk <- diagnostic_markers(ex$genotypes, ex$groups, "species1", "species2", locus = ex$locus)
sc <- hybrid_scores(ex$genotypes, mk)
table(ex$groups, classify_hybrids(sc)$class)
#>           
#>            BC2_species1 F2 later pure1 pure2
#>   site_A              0 17    13     0     0
#>   site_B              3  0    27     0     0
#>   species1            0  0     0    20     0
#>   species2            0  0     0     0    20
cl <- classify_hybrids(sc, error = "estimate", genotypes = orient_genotypes(ex$genotypes, mk),
                       markers = mk)
attr(cl, "error")
#> [1] 5e-04
